listing.name: Command & Conquer: Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn & Dune 2000 / OpenRA (OpenRA)
listing.summary: Explore Command & Conquer: Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn & Dune 2000 / OpenRA (OpenRA) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Choose the game you want to play
steps.instruction: For 64-bit Windows, use the official stable portable ZIP in a separate folder. It contains three different players: RedAlert.exe for Red Alert, TiberianDawn.exe for Tiberian Dawn, and Dune2000.exe for Dune 2000. Choose that game executable when finishing setup; OpenRA.Server and OpenRA.Utility are not the normal players. Portcove leaves this choice to you and does not run a discovered helper. Alternatively use the upstream Windows installer, the game-specific Linux AppImage, or the macOS disk image, then register the prepared player. An AppImage or disk image needs its own upstream platform instructions, not ZIP extraction.

steps.title: Let your chosen game finish its own content setup
steps.instruction: Choose Play explicitly, then follow that player’s content installation screen. It can offer upstream downloads or import from your own original game media; available content differs between Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn and Dune 2000. Portcove does not run these content tools during discovery or supply original media.

steps.title: Keep the OpenRA profile and current copy
steps.instruction: Updates come from OpenRA. Install a new release separately and keep your current copy usable while checking it; stable releases and playtests are different choices. Saves, settings, downloaded content, maps, replays and screenshots normally use %APPDATA%/OpenRA on Windows, ~/.config/openra on Linux, or ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA on macOS. An existing legacy profile may be reused. A Support directory beside the engine, or an explicit support-directory setting, changes this location. Back up the profile you actually use separately; Portcove does not manage this runtime or promise Backup/Rollback for it. An older engine may not read newer saves/mods. Custom mods use their own matching engine/runtime instructions.
